details: CONFIRMED by reading and reproduced. In a scratch clone at b2fbb15 with one old-shape item committed on top:
test_round_trip fails (AssertionError at tests/test_queue.py:491) and `bin/relay queue check` exits 1 naming the file.
The UPDATE answered design F4 with "rerun the migration after taking master", but the rerun is a manual step with no reminder:
taking master with only inert files needs no new gate or mark, and the hook at this merge is master's old code, so no code in
this change can stop this one merge; it needs a step in the front's merge procedure (run `bin/relay queue check` in the worktree
right after the last take of master, immediately before `git merge`). For every later merge, the new step_queue could parse all
queue files at the branch tip (about 60 small files), which turns a red round-trip test into a refusal that names the command.
MIGRATE_HINT "on this branch" is also misleading when `relay queue` shows the residue on master.
evidence: git log --oneline HEAD..master -> (empty today; the window opens with any queue write on master before the merge)
.relay/queue/late-old-item.json: old shape (state, found, closed_by): run `relay queue migrate` on this branch ; check exit 1
failing_case: Until this branch merges, master's queue code is step 1, whose `relay queue add` writes the old shape ("state": "open", "found",
"closed_by"). Sequence: the branch is migrated, gated and checked; the front runs `relay queue add` on master (old shape, x.json);
the merge hook says "behind master, take master first"; `git merge master` brings x.json in; .relay/queue/** is inert, so mark and
gate stay valid and nobody reruns the migration; the merge hook at this merge is master's step-1 code, which accepts both shapes
and only looks at the range anyway. After the merge, master holds x.json in the old shape:
- `relay queue` lists it as "malformed: old shape ...: run `relay queue migrate` on this branch" (there is no branch: migrate only
rewrites a checkout, nothing lands it on master);
- take/ip/drop/release of x refuse;
- tests/test_queue.py::TestFormat::test_round_trip_is_byte_identical_for_every_seed_item reads the committed queue files, so the
gate of every branch that takes master fails "library tests" for a reason outside its change;
- the new step_queue checks only files the range adds or modifies, so later merges do not name the cause either.
It is not hypothetical: commit 7329fb0 on this branch ("migrate items landed on master") had to convert
principles-become-a-relay-rule-other-projects-ca, landed on master in the old shape after the first migration.
Expected: the merge does not happen while the branch tip holds an old-shape file, or the residue is converted and named at once.
fix_hint: Write the pre-merge step into the front's procedure for this merge (after the last `git merge master`: `bin/relay queue check -C
<worktree>`; on failure `bin/relay queue migrate` and commit). In step_queue, also parse every .relay/queue/*.json and done/*.json
at the branch tip (not only the range) and refuse an old-shape one with MIGRATE_HINT; a merge.test.sh case with an old-shape file
arriving through master. Optionally say "on a branch, then merge it" in MIGRATE_HINT.
pass_cases: - Branch tip with one old-shape .relay/queue/x.json that came from master (not in the range): the step that runs before the
merge (the front's `bin/relay queue check -C <worktree>`, written into the merge procedure, or the new step_queue checking every
queue file at the branch tip) refuses, naming x.json and `relay queue migrate`; after `bin/relay queue migrate` + commit it passes.
- Branch tip where every queue file has the new shape (today's HEAD): allowed, `relay queue check` prints "every queue item file is
- A dropped done/ file in the new shape that arrived through master (merge.test.sh T15n2): still not judged, allowed.
- An old-shape done/ file added by the range (T15n3): still refused naming `relay queue migrate`.
reason: plugins/core/tests/merge.test.sh T15n4 passed (old-shape item via master refused naming migration); T15n2 dropped-via-master allowed, T15n3 old-shape refused still pass; step_queue now ls-tree's the tip.
findings.summary: an old-shape item written on master after the last migrate run reaches master unconverted at the merge; nothing refuses it and every later gate turns red

details: CONFIRMED by running check() on queue-analytics-views.json with taken_by="", test="" and dropped_why=[]: each returns [].
The rules use bool(...) where the design asks for null. Size: 5.
failing_case: An open item with "taken_at": null, "taken_by": "" (or "test": "" with "closed_at": null, or "dropped_why": [] with
"dropped_at": null): check(slug, data, "open") returns [] today. The brief: "taken_by, test, dropped_why become null when absent
(no more "")". Writers write null, so only a hand edit or a stray tool produces it; readers that test `is None` would differ from
those that test truthiness.
fix_hint: Refuse a str key ("taken_by", "test") that is "" and a dropped_why that is [] (null when absent), with one table row each in the
pass_cases: - taken_at null, taken_by "" -> refused ("taken_by is null or a branch name").
- closed_at null, test "" -> refused; dropped_at null, dropped_why [] -> refused.
- An open item from `relay queue add` (all null) -> accepted.
- A taken item with taken_by "wt/x" and taken_at set -> accepted.
reason: tests/test_queue.py TestNewShape test_each_new_rule_refuses rows for taken_by "", test "", dropped_why [] pass; check() diff in lib/relay_queue.py:120-130; copies identical.
findings.summary: check() accepts "" for taken_by and test and [] for dropped_why when the event is absent; the design says null
